title: Definitive F-KT15 Solver-Service Transaction Composition Canonical Admission Architecture Audit

invariants.assessment: One SWAP kernel remains the production authority; F-KT15 composes a solver service into the existing kernel/runtime path.
No kernel file I/O contract is introduced; legacy binding remains outside the kernel contract.
Parameters, committed state, forcing, numerical policy and results remain separate contracts.
No new persistent column state is introduced by the 17-path KT15 composition.
Hydraulic trial results and solver workspace remain worker/trial local; no scratch persistence is introduced.
Worker-local capsules are qualified for 1, 2, 4 and 8 logical workers; no per-column heavy solver owner is introduced.
Checkpoint/trial/retry/commit/rollback semantics are preserved; rejected typed trials do not publish candidate physical arrays.
No committed-state ownership inversion or warm-start persistence is introduced.
No calendar assumption is introduced; current-canonical restart replay uses generic non-calendar t0/t1 windows.
No fixed coupling-window duration is introduced.
Transaction and interface result transport remain explicit kernel/runtime functionality.
No change weakens the head/flux interface contract; this admission does not claim full MODFLOW coupling.
Hard water-mass checks remain mandatory and are replayed for the restricted production surface regimes.
Accepted local terminal qbot sensitivity is transported as first-class trial output only for the qualified smooth surface-flux route, using the same factorization.
Sensitivity qualification uses one same-factorization backsolve and no second nonlinear sensitivity trajectory.
Worker isolation is explicitly replayed; the composition introduces no heavyweight solver instance per logical column.
No one-to-one MODFLOW-cell ownership assumption is introduced.
Deep-vadose remains outside SWAP and is not touched by this admission.
No component-transition water storage or accounting rule is changed.
The soil-water solver contract remains an interface; this admission does not make the runtime depend on one hidden solver implementation.
Existing SWAP process physics are reused; no duplicate crop, ET, drainage or surface physics is introduced.
Solver internals are consumed through the soil-water solver/result contracts; other modules do not acquire HeadCalc internal-array ownership.
Physical route restrictions remain explicit and are not silently changed by numerical policy.
No throughput claim or unbounded fallback policy is added; failed admitted solves request retry and fail closed.
Reference/full-accuracy authorities remain available and unchanged; no reference tree mutation is admitted.
Worker diagnostics and typed trial-result metadata preserve visibility of solve route, retry and sensitivity outcome.
Optional functionality remains conditional; KT15 does not force optional physical state allocation.
Runtime/coupler composition ownership is unchanged; no tile fraction, MODFLOW topology or transfer-zone relation enters the SWAP kernel.
The admitted path is generic in t0/t1 and carries no midnight, one-day, .swp or direct-MODFLOW assumption.
This explicit audit plus exact-source and replay gates evaluates all architecture invariants for the canonical admission image.

hard_nonclaims: No interface tangent claim outside the restricted smooth surface-flux route.
No active-root, macropore, frost, SWDRA=2, time-dependent PONDMX or nonlinear-runoff typed-route admission.
